newsitem.title: UK: Hambros/Guinness fund venture may seek listing.
newsitem.headline: Hambros/Guinness fund venture may seek listing.

text.p: The merged Guinness Flight Hambro Asset Management could seek a listing within three years, the company's new deputy chairman said on Monday.

Howard Flight, current joint managing director of Guinness Flight, told Reuters the deal made provision for a listing. "Certainly after 2000, if management wanted to float the business then it would float."
Hambros said on Sunday it would merge its Hambros Fund Management (HFM) unit with Guinness Flight Global Asset Management -- a move bringing combined funds under management to 9.3 billion stg.
He said the deal had come at an opportune time, with greater acceptance of new players in the UK pension fund industry following recent adverse publicity at some bigger rivals.

"The timing of aspiring to do this is not unpropitious because...one way or the other a few people have slightly bashed their shins and we get the sort of vibes that the actuarial body would quite welcome one or two more players coming up."
Analysts said the deal could raise speculation about possible mergers among the smaller managers following months of talk about the bigger independents.

Sunday's statement said substantial cost savings would be made through the cutting of marketing, pricing and administration costs in shareholder services and through combined central operational functions such as accounting and personnel.
On completion of the deal, Guinness Mahon Holdings Plc and Hambros will each hold a 42.5 percent stake in the new firm, with around 15.0 percent held by management.
But Hambros added that options schemes could push management's stake up to 30 percent when appropriate targets are met.

HFM managing director Andrew Martin Smith said the new company would seek to build its principal areas of focus, currently managed currency funds, Asian equity funds, and cash and fixed interest management.
He said the core areas were likely to become increasingly popular in coming months amid concern about current price levels in the U.S. and other key equity markets.
UBS fund industry analyst Martin Cross told Reuters the merger of Hambros fund management operation came as no surprise.
"Hambros would have been the first to admit that the scale of their fund management operations was not optimal," he said.
Cross said there may be some speculation following the news that there will be further restructuring of Hambros' operations, which could be reflected in the share price.
"The market may start to speculate on that...I tend to think that Hambros share price is still undervalued," he said, adding that the deal should help the market rating of Hambros shares.
He dismissed criticism of the deal from Regent Pacific Group Ltd, which said the merger was "a very bad deal" for Hambros.

"They have approximately six billion pounds or 10 billion U.S. dollars under management and Guinness Flight has one-third of that figure, and yet after the merger they will end up with an equivalent position and Hambros will not be in control," said Jim Mellon, managing director of Regent Pacific, which holds slightly less than four percent of Hambros' stock.
Cross said the more telling figure would be the revenues that each group was bringing to the new venture.
The companies said Guinness Flight would bring in 25.5 million stg and Hambros 11 million.
Following months of merger speculation about some of the bigger fund managers, analysts say smaller managers could come under the spotlight.
"Smaller fund management companies are more likely to have something to happen to them than big ones," Cross said.
